body.estimand_functional: \(q_0=4+\delta\), \(b_\lambda=(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star)_+^{1/2}\), and \(\widehat\mu_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^T}\!\left\{\widehat U(\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat U_{S_c})^{-1}\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat\nu_c\right\}\). The unconditional upper guarantees on every nonempty shell are \(\mathcal R_N\le\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2,C_0/(Ns_N^2)\}\) and \(\mathcal W_{N,\alpha}\le\min\{b_\lambda,C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\}\). The robust moment inversion intersects its profiled rectangle with \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\), and both procedures retain their total fallbacks. A frontier-scale testing pair on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open; \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient, not necessary in the zero-target boundary class.

sampling_model.design: Observational short panel with deterministic cohort-specific untreated masks \(S_c\) and independent cross-sectional sampling. The model analyzed here is the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error intersection subclass of the broader Lei--Ross environment, not that full stochastic class.
sampling_model.treatment: For cohort \(c\), recovery uses \(J_cY_i(0)\). The untreated factor law has conditional mean-zero, loading-uncorrelated, spherical errors; treated outcomes are outside the recovery functional and may be appended without changing it.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \(p_c\ge p_\star>0\) and every \(S_c\) contains at least three coordinates. Identification strength is the observable relation margin \(s(P)\), while feasible target size is bounded by \(b_\lambda=(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/(4+\delta)}-2v_\star)_+^{1/2}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cohort means and covariances feed covariance PCA and APM least squares, clipped to \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\). Robust joint-moment blocks feed a profile-recentered compact-model inversion whose rectangle is intersected with the same box. Both procedures are total, and the results are unconditional upper guarantees rather than lower-frontier claims.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 establishes \(O_3\) acceptance as a sufficient mask condition for factor-plane identification.
Their Theorems 1 and 2 supply rank-two deterministic sampling count conditions for generic subspace identification and matrix completion.
Their Theorems 1--3 provide entrywise intervals and an instance-wise lower bound for a growing staggered-block matrix model.
Their weak-factor results derive minimax and honesty costs when factor strength or factor number is uncertain.
Their paper establishes uniformly valid identification-robust tests and confidence sets across weak, semi-strong, and strong sequences in broad extremum models.
Their Theorem 1 and corollaries give deterministic necessary and sufficient conditions for generic coordinate-subspace identifiability.
Their Theorem 1 bounds canonical-projection subspace error by projection noise divided by a relation singular value.
Their Theorems 10 and 12 identify generic entry completability with closure in the determinantal matroid through Jacobian row span.
Their Theorem 1.8 and pebble algorithms characterize and recognize sparse hypergraphs.

body.tldr: Short panels with systematic missing outcomes require gluing cohort-specific covariance eigenspaces before missing untreated means become causal functionals. A deterministic smallest-two anchor convention maps every mask to the published rank-two count certificate, with pebble recognition and extraction as background. Certificate acceptance yields an explicit complete-observed-law map; certificate failure yields generic factor-plane nonuniqueness but not model-wide causal-target nonidentification. For the stochastic class studied here, put \(q_0=4+\delta\) and \(b_\lambda=(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star)_+^{1/2}\). Covariance PCA has unconditional squared-risk upper bound \(\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2,C_0/(Ns_N^2)\}\), and robust profile-recentered inversion has uniform coverage with maximal half-width at most \(\min\{b_\lambda,C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\}\). The four-mask witness shows strict geometric containment beyond \(O_3\). No universal lower frontier or necessity claim is made: \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient, while an allowed boundary class has \(b_\lambda=0\) and zero target throughout.

project_justification.gap: Published matrix-completion count criteria and pebble algorithms certify generic rank-two geometry, while Lei and Ross provide an \(O_3\)-sufficient APM analysis. They do not give the complete-observed-law causal transport proved here, nor the radius-adaptive finite-sample upper guarantees \(\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2,C_0/(Ns_N^2)\}\) and \(\min\{b_\lambda,C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\}\). The stochastic class here is not literally the full Lei--Ross class: the overlap is only the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error intersection subclass, and \(O_3\) is used geometrically.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies fixed-\(T\) causal recovery under deterministic cohort masks, separating generic factor-plane certification from causal-target identification and separating singular-margin instability from the smaller target radius forced by the primitive moment budget. It combines an explicit observed-law functional, strict \(O_3\) containment, covariance--PCA risk upper bounds, and finite-moment uniformly honest moment inversion.
project_justification.fill: The paper takes the published count and pebble results as inputs, proves positive causal transport when the certificate passes, and records only factor-plane ambiguity when it fails. It derives \(\|m_c\|_2\le b_\lambda\) from the frozen moment and covariance restrictions, clips estimation and inversion to the resulting target box, and proves radius-adaptive unconditional upper guarantees. Nondegenerate same-shell testing pairs and corresponding lower risk and width frontiers remain open.

body.related_work: Published deterministic rank-two sampling criteria and sparse-hypergraph pebble algorithms provide the geometric certificate, while determinantal-matroid work explains generic completion. Lei and Ross are the closest econometric comparator, but the stochastic class in this paper is not their full class: only the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error intersection subclass is shared. Their \(O_3\) procedure is used as a geometric sufficient screen; the masks \(123,145,256,346\) show strict certificate inclusion. The distinct causal contribution is the complete-observed-law mean functional and the radius-adaptive upper analysis. Projection perturbation results explain reciprocal-margin behavior but do not furnish a legal target-separating experiment under the frozen primitives. Growing staggered-matrix inference, weak-factor honesty theory, and general identification-robust inference likewise do not close the missing nondegenerate same-shell lower construction. The \(\operatorname{apm}\) Veneto counterfactual-wage workflow and \(\operatorname{fect}\) are consumers, not assertions that their full maintained models coincide with this class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Certificate failure proves generic factor-plane nonuniqueness but not distinct causal targets under the frozen primitive class. At the nonempty-model moment boundary \(b_\lambda=0\), equivalently \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v_\star)^{(4+\delta)/2}\), the strengthened boundary argument forces \(H_c=v_\star I_2\), \(m_c=0\), and zero errors almost surely, so every causal target is zero. Shell nonemptiness alone therefore supplies neither target separation nor primitive interior slack. Construction of a nondegenerate frontier-scale testing pair and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open. The covariance--PCA and robust-inversion results are unconditional upper guarantees; numerical certification of the compact profile optimization is outside the theorem.
body.honest_scope: The deterministic anchor convention, generic rank-two count criterion, and pebble algorithms are published geometric background. The paper claims positive causal transport from certificate acceptance, strict geometric containment beyond \(O_3\), and radius-adaptive unconditional upper guarantees for the stated spherical-error factor subclass. It does not identify this stochastic class with the full Lei--Ross model. The point estimator clips to \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\), and robust moment inversion intersects its profiled rectangle with the same box while retaining total fallbacks. No minimax lower frontier, honest-width lower frontier, causal-target converse on certificate failure, or necessity of \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is claimed.
body.interpretation: The relation margin \(s(P)\) measures the stability of gluing local factor planes, whereas \(b_\lambda\) measures how far the primitive moment budget permits cohort loading means, and hence counterfactual means, to move. The two restrictions act through different minima: sampling instability contributes \(1/(Ns_N^2)\) to squared risk and \(1/(\sqrt N s_N)\) to half-width, while the target box contributes \(4b_\lambda^2\) and \(b_\lambda\), respectively. Thus a small relation margin is a conservative warning, not an impossibility certificate when the target radius is itself small or zero.
